q: All five resistors are identical. The voltmeter reads $1.0\ \text{V}$. What is the voltage across the battery?

lines.say: Five identical resistors, and the voltmeter reads one volt. What's the voltage across the battery?
This is a real engineering admissions test question. Pause and have a go!
Okay! {vm}The voltmeter is across just this one resistor, so it has one volt.
Its twin is identical, {bl}so that's one volt too, {br}and two volts across the whole bottom branch.
The top resistor is in parallel, {top}so it gets two volts as well.
Now the current. {cur}On top, two volts across R gives two over R. {cur2}Along the bottom, it's one over R. {cur3}So three over R flows through each outside resistor.
Three over R, times R, {out}is three volts each.
Add it all up: {sum}three, plus two, plus three. {ans}Eight volts! It's E.
If you said four, {trap}you used one volt for the whole parallel bit. Classic trap!
